key_insight: CT-Navigator uses progressive visual exploration and tool invocation to ground CT question answering in traceable image evidence rather than one-step scan interpretation.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support more inspectable CT interpretation workflows, but clinical utility and safety are not established by the reported benchmarks.
method: Uses a generalist multimodal model to navigate CT scans hierarchically, from whole scans to slices and regions of interest.
Invokes radiology tools and learns from 8,904 visual chain-of-thought trajectories.
Refines its policy with reinforcement learning on 33,219 questions, prioritizing informative training signals.
evidence_signal: On the new 7,000-question CTNavi-Bench, CT-Navigator achieved 79.50% accuracy, with a reported 17.59% improvement over the strongest baseline, and showed generalization across three external CT benchmarks.
watch_item: Benchmark accuracy and traceable outputs do not establish reliable clinical reasoning; prospective validation and tool-error assessment remain important.
paper_title: CT-Navigator: Towards Interpretable and Generalizable CT Understanding through Agentic Perception and Tool-Invocation
